evals.prompt: Formalize these requirements as SBVR: Premium customers may return items within 60 days; standard customers may return items within 30 days; final-sale items cannot be returned.
evals.expected_output: Creates SBVR vocabulary, fact types, and behavioral/definitional rules that preserve the stated return windows without assuming they must use the bundled policy-reference convention.
expectations: The answer separates vocabulary, fact types, and rules.
The stated 60-day and 30-day values are preserved; policy concepts are introduced only if configurability or the selected house profile justifies them.
Rules use valid SBVR keywords such as obligatory, prohibited, permitted, necessary, or impossible.
The answer avoids system-as-actor and technical implementation terms.
The answer does not present the bundled validator or Markdown profile as an SBVR requirement.

evals.prompt: Audit this house-profile SBVR spec for threshold leakage, undefined terms, and weak modality.
evals.expected_output: A review/audit report with concrete SBVR findings and fixes.
expectations: Identifies undefined or inconsistently used terms.
Flags threshold leakage according to the stated house profile rather than claiming all SBVR rules forbid digits.
Checks necessity/obligation/prohibition wording.
Separates validator-checkable issues from semantic review.

evals.prompt: Produce canonical YAML output for this small vocabulary and rule set.
evals.expected_output: A structured YAML-oriented SBVR output following the skill's optional house-profile schema.
expectations: Uses a structured vocabulary/rules schema.
Preserves terms, fact types, and rule identifiers.
Keeps rule text controlled and unambiguous.
Mentions validation command where relevant.

evals.prompt: Update this SBVR rule set by adding two rules and renumbering safely.
evals.expected_output: An update workflow that preserves IDs where possible and uses dry-run renumbering before mutation.
expectations: Explains update impact before renumbering.
Uses or recommends renumber.py --dry-run before applying changes.
Keeps cross-references consistent.
Reports validation results or limitations.

evals.prompt: Run the SBVR validator and explain which findings are mechanical versus needing human business review.
evals.expected_output: A house-profile validator review that does not overstate mechanical validation or general SBVR compliance.
expectations: Describes validator scope and exit codes.
Separates syntax/structure findings from semantic policy questions.
Provides remediation steps.
Does not claim the validator proves business correctness or general SBVR compliance.

evals.prompt: Create an SBVR for a fictional streaming service replacing its legacy platform. The scenario includes subscribers, subscriptions, plan tiers, billing, payments, content licensing and licensor statements. The discovery notes name two example systems, Archive Billing and Legacy Rights, and describe a separate migration project. Mid-cycle proration is unresolved.
evals.expected_output: A business-meaning SBVR that extracts and classifies candidates before defining vocabulary, models status lifecycles, keeps the real business concepts, and excludes project/implementation/source-system noise.
expectations: Extracts and classifies candidates (or applies a belongs-in-SBVR filter) before defining vocabulary, rather than promoting every noun.
Keeps supported business concepts such as subscriber, subscription, plan, invoice, payment, content license, and licensor statement.
Models status-bearing entities (subscription, payment, content license) with the status-enumeration-transition pattern, not as permanent subtypes.
Excludes Archive Billing, Legacy Rights, and migration from core vocabulary unless a business rule directly depends on them, treating them as source/implementation/project artifacts.
Treats unresolved mid-cycle proration as an open/deferred topic rather than inventing a rule, and treats plan tier as a changeable attribute rather than a permanent subtype.
Separates confirmed rules from open/deferred discovery items and surfaces the exclusions for review.

evals.prompt: Create an SBVR for a library loan process with clear borrower, item, loan, due date, renewal, fine, and hold rules.
evals.expected_output: A normal SBVR for a clean domain that does not over-filter legitimate business concepts.
expectations: Produces normal vocabulary, fact types, and rules for the loan domain.
Does not over-filter or drop legitimate business concepts (borrower, item, loan, due date, renewal, fine, hold).
Preserves stated loan periods or fine rates; uses policy terms only when configurability or the selected artifact profile justifies them.
Applies the extract/filter passes lightly given the domain is clean and well-specified.

evals.prompt: Create an SBVR for a billing process that syncs with a payment processor, CRM, and ERP.
evals.expected_output: An SBVR that keeps business billing concepts and rules while moving integration plumbing out of the vocabulary.
expectations: Keeps business concepts and rules around invoice, payment, customer, allocation, and reconciliation.
Moves payment processor, CRM, ERP, API, sync job, and webhook details out of the SBVR unless a business rule directly depends on them.
Distinguishes business vocabulary from integration/implementation artifacts via classification or a belongs-in-SBVR filter.
Avoids irrelevant implementation plumbing in business rules without treating every technical term as automatically invalid.

evals.prompt: In SBVR, what is a fact type? Give me one example for an order domain.
evals.expected_output: A concise explanation and one example, without forcing a full vocabulary document, house profile, validator run, or checklist.
expectations: Explains that a fact type represents a kind of relationship or proposition involving concepts.
Gives one relevant order-domain example.
Does not force the optional Markdown/YAML profile or validation workflow onto an explanatory question.

evals.expected_output: An SBVR document grounded in the fictional code, with vocabulary, fact types, definitional and behavioral rules, code-derived observations, and open or deferred policy questions.
expectations: Finds the status, preview, maturity, and sandbox guards in the supplied code before formalizing their meaning.
Grounds playback rules in preview formats, evaluation/paid/retry access, and the G/PG youth rating limit.
Distinguishes definitional rules from behavioral rules and keeps sandbox HTTP responses in implementation evidence.
Labels access with a missing profile and handling of unknown youth ratings as code observations pending policy confirmation.
Records grace-period expiry, refunds, and tier changes as open or deferred questions without inventing business rules.
